title: RegMean statistics to Mirror merge coefficients
hypothesis: On aligned synthetic layer deltas, a low-dimensional shared-basis coefficient solved from RegMean sufficient statistics preserves the full RegMean objective within 5% while reducing complete serialized merge state, including statistics, by at least 25% versus full RegMean and native projected RegMean.
physical_object: shared rank-4 delta basis and source task deltas for one synthetic linear layer
mirror_coordinate: per-request coefficient vector solved by minimizing the summed RegMean quadratic objective in the shared basis
logical_multiplicity: 12 synthetic merged outputs from 8 source tasks
controls: native projected RegMean solve with same basis and coefficients

development.selection_metric: per-request normalized RegMean objective, complete payload bytes, solve-work proxy

fresh.reason: development mechanism screen determines failure; audit is not opened after a frozen development failure

paid_objects: source task coefficients or dense deltas

success_gate: Every request objective <=1.05x full RegMean; complete serialized bundle <=75% of both full RegMean and native projected solve; solve-work proxy <=1.25x.
failure_gate: Any predeclared quality/storage/compute gate miss or exact payload/function alias with native projected RegMean is FAIL for Mirror-specific value. Gate definitions were fixed before inspecting dev outcomes.
boundaries: Synthetic linear-layer mechanism only; no trained neural network, pretrained model or natural benchmark.
Gram and cross-statistics are generated synthetic sufficient statistics; their task acquisition cost is not measured, but their persistent deployment bytes are fully charged.
No audit/fresh result, GPU runtime, language quality or capacity claim.
